title: NEMO
organization: Purdue Trace Labs / Humanoid Robotics Club
summary: NEMO is a small-scale humanoid robot designed to mimic human-like proportions, created for research into bipedal locomotion. Standing at approximately 3 feet tall, NEMO was engineered for rapid iteration and practicality, utilizing deep reinforcement learning to develop a functional walking gait.
lede: Designing the physical platform for a student-built bipedal humanoid—and the iteration loop required to make it walk.

title: Third Thumb
summary: Designed a 3-DOF prosthetic 'third thumb' with pin-jointed phalanges and a wearable hand interface. The prototype integrated a a servo-driven wire-tensioning system mounted onto the hand and wrist for responsive thumb actuation.
lede: A compact wearable mechanism at the intersection of human factors, mechanical design, and control.

title: VTOL Aircraft
summary: Supported the development of a VTOL (Vertical Take-Off and Landing) drone capable of seamlessly transitioning from vertical to horizontal flight. I helped enhance the structural integrity and optimizing the aerodynamic performance of the aircraft.
lede: Developing an aircraft architecture that transitions between vertical lift and forward flight around a defined mission.

title: H.A.R.R.Y.
summary: Developed H.A.R.R.Y., a mobile aluminum humanoid robot designed to aid individuals with mobility challenges. This prototype successfully demonstrated its ability to elevate its chassis, perform complex arm movements, and grip and lift objects, culminating in a presentation of its capabilities to industry professionals.
lede: An early robotics project centered on translating human movement into a physical prototype.

title: VEX Competition Robot
summary: As the team captain, I led the development of a competitive robot for the VEX Spin Up competition. The robot was engineered for high-speed disk intake and shooting, along with a custom expansion mechanism, leading to a championship win at the NJ TSA Championships and qualification for both VEX Nationals and World Championships.
lede: Designing mechanisms under strict game, time, packaging, and reliability constraints.
